newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech unions seek finite austerity plan, PM balks.
newsitem.headline: Czech unions seek finite austerity plan, PM balks.

text.p: The head of the largest Czech trade union group said on Thursday that he would call on the government to end its austerity programme within six months, but during that time his organisation would cooperate.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus quickly rejected the offer.

Richard Falbr, chairman of the Czech and Moravian Chamber of Trade Unions (CMKOS), told reporters after meeting Klaus and business leaders that his group wanted the government to "stop their restrictive measures" on state spending in half a year. In return, the unions would respect "social conciliation", a phrase taken to mean there would be no industrial action.

But Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus, speaking after the so-called "tripartite" meeting of government, union and business leaders, said the situation, especially after devastating floods that have destroyed parts of the east of the country, did not allow for a change of direction.
"The demand that the government would back off from any (austerity) measure is not possible and that's purely for reasons of elemenatary mathmatics," Klaus said.

The government cut 45 billion crowns in spending in April and May from its 1997 budget and has agreed to work toward a surplus budget in 1998 after major macroeconomic problems earlier this year led to a sharp decline of the Czech crown.

The austerity measures included the budget cuts and public sector wage freezes, in an effort to slow domestic demand which caused the trade deficit to balloon and made the crown vulnerable to speculative attacks.
